content:
You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Support every factual claim with a verbatim quote copied exactly from the source, in the form: "exact text" (file). Never paraphrase inside the quotation marks. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no citation.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- Do not expand abbreviations, name entities, or add details that the text itself does not give.
- Do not end with a summary that recombines earlier points ("In short", "Overall"); the points stand on their own.
- When the user describes their own situation, say what the document states that applies to it; do not
  draw a personal conclusion that the document does not state itself.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

Paraphrase the measures the company has taken to improve the quality of life of cows.

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

name: read
content:
1	In 2022, 50 farms in Ben & Jerry’s Northeast dairy supply chain participated in the Milk with
     2	Dignity Program. They employed over 200 farmworkers covered through the program. During 2022,
     3	participating farm owners and farmworkers made over 300 inquiries to MDSC, 25% of which related to
     4	workplace health and safety, 22% to wages and related issues, 12% to schedules and rest, and 18% to
     5	housing conditions. Additionally, since the program launched, over $4.4 million from Ben & Jerry’s
     6	has supported farms’ improvements to working and housing conditions, including $2.9 million in
     7	raises to meet minimum wages (which reached $12.55 per hour in Vermont in 2022) and $1.49 million in
     8	bonuses, paid vacation and sick time, housing improvements, new personal protective equipment, and
     9	other safety improvements. Farms have continued to make concrete progress toward full compliance
    10	with standards such as the rights to at least eight consecutive hours of per workday, one day of per
    11	week, and comprehensive occupational safety and health protections.
    12	
    13	Excellent Life for Cows The care for dairy cows is critically important and we rely on independent
    14	third-party standards to advance animal care in our supply. In 2021 and 2022, we audited farms to
    15	both our Caring Dairy Standard and the Global Animal Partnership (GAP) Dairy care standard. The
    16	audits identifed specifc opportunities to improve care while also highlighting industry-level
    17	barriers that may impede broader adoption of higher-level certifcations. Our farm partners are
    18	interested in continuous improvements with approximately 20% becoming GAP certifed, a not
    19	insignifcant step above standard industry performance, after undergoing the rigorous audits.
    20	
    21	Regenerative and Circular Agriculture Our farm partners recognize the growing pressure to fnd viable
    22	solutions to the climate crisis and are thoughtful and engaged collaborators in trialing new on-farm
    23	management practices to track and increase carbon sequestration, biodiversity, and build soil
    24	health. In preparation for a deeper dive into low carbon dairy, we conducted individual farm
    25	greenhouse gas (GHG) footprints using the Cool Farm Tool. 2022 also marked the third, and last, year
    26	of Prove It Projects carried out by Ben & Jerry’s Caring Dairy Farmer Innovators. Prove It Projects
    27	were designed to provide farmers with insights and opportunities to test run practices in
    28	regenerative concepts in the real-life laboratory of their own farms. The practices farmers “proved”
    29	to have value are then adopted into their own farm management and shared with the broader Ben &
    30	Jerry’s community. In 2022, each of the 27 Farmer Innovators selected two on-farm research projects
    31	from a list of 11 previously identifed projects, implementing a total of 54 projects. Several
    32	practices farmers tested stood out as providing benefcial outcomes:
    33	
    34	Nitrogen inhibitors showed advantages in yield and reduced input needs. • Changes to grazing
    35	management could help increase on-farm forage and cut production costs. • Multi-species cover crops
    36	were more viable with diferent planting techniques. • Farmers are still addressing habitat
    37	biodiversity, in what is a multi-year endeavor. In all, the three years of Prove It Projects have
    38	provided farmers with valuable insights while also informing the next iteration of Ben & Jerry’s
    39	farmer innovation pilots in hopes to drive Low Carbon Dairy farming.

Based on `doc.txt`, the measures the company describes for improving the quality of life of cows are limited to the "Excellent Life for Cows" section:

1. **Reliance on third-party standards:** The company says it depends on outside standards to advance animal care, stating "we rely on independent third-party standards to advance animal care in our supply" (doc.txt).

2. **Auditing farms against two care standards:** In 2021 and 2022, the company "audited farms to both our Caring Dairy Standard and the Global Animal Partnership (GAP) Dairy care standard" (doc.txt).

3. **Using audit findings to identify improvements:** "The audits identifed specifc opportunities to improve care while also highlighting industry-level barriers that may impede broader adoption of higher-level certifcations" (doc.txt).

4. **Farm partners pursuing certification:** "Our farm partners are interested in continuous improvements with approximately 20% becoming GAP certifed, a not insignifcant step above standard industry performance, after undergoing the rigorous audits" (doc.txt).

The document does not describe any other specific measures (such as housing, feeding, or veterinary practices) taken to improve the cows' quality of life; the remaining sections of the file concern farmworker conditions under the Milk with Dignity Program and regenerative/circular agriculture practices.
